title: Conversational KV Lifecycle - Product Brief
author: Priya Kapoor
content:
Summary
-------
This product brief outlines the Conversational Key-Value (KV) Lifecycle initiative: a product-facing specification and playbook that defines how conversation state (short-term KV caches, pinned context, and persisted session state) is created, shaped, retained, and expired across Redwood's hosting tiers (Hosted, Dedicated, Private). The primary goal is to give customers predictable economics and privacy guarantees while preserving conversational quality for multi-turn applications.

Goals
-----
- Provide a predictable, opinionated lifecycle for KV state that balances latency, cost, and contextual fidelity.
- Enable per-tenant policy controls for retention, privacy, and snapshotting that map to commercial tiers.
- Reduce token re-generation and downstream compute by maximizing safe cache reuse.
- Offer clear operational controls and diagnostics for SRE and customer success teams.

Scope
-----
In scope:
- Short-term KV caching inside the serving runtime (prefix/KV cache) and lifecycle policy hooks exposed via API and Console.
- Per-route and per-tenant retention profiles (ephemeral, session, pinned, persisted).
- Auditable deletion and export flows for compliance.
- Interaction with fallback variants and quantized model variants to ensure compatibility.

Out of scope (for this phase):
- Long-term vector store lifecycle for embeddings (covered in embeddings-retention-tiering).
- Deep archival integration with third-party object stores (planned as add-on).

Background and motivation
-------------------------
Customers building multi-turn assistants frequently trade off two things: user experience (long context, high quality) and unit economics (cost of re-generating or re-encoding prefix state). Currently, customers either:
1) allow the runtime to manage caches automatically with opaque retention semantics, or
2) push lifecycle to application logic which increases engineering overhead and inconsistency.

We observed three common support patterns that motivate a product-level lifecycle:
- Unexpected token costs when an ephemeral conversation is retained longer than intended.
- Privacy/audit requests where tenants are unsure if a user's KV-derived state still exists.
- Suboptimal fallback behavior when a compacted/quantized model variant expects different KV shapes.

Design principles
------------------
1. Explicit policies are first-class: the platform exposes named retention profiles that are composable with rollout policies (canary, A/B).
2. Backwards-compatible defaults: new behavior should not change existing hosted customers' economics by default.
3. Privacy-by-design: retention profiles map to deletion guarantees and export hooks for compliance.
4. Observable and actionable: every retention decision is surfaced in Console and telemetry with clear attribution.

Retention profiles (recommended set)
------------------------------------
- ephemeral: TTL 5 minutes (default for public playgrounds and unauthenticated flows).
- session: TTL 2 hours of inactivity, persisted during the session lifetime.
- conversation-pinned: manual pin by SDK/API, TTL 30 days, exportable by tenant.
- persisted-archive: explicit customer opt-in for long-term storage, governed by a separate storage contract and controls.

Each profile defines: TTL, deletion window, export format (JSON/NDJSON), per-tenant overrides, and cost-class (S, M, L) which maps to billing buckets.

API and Console surface
-----------------------
API additions (examples):
- POST /v1/conversations/{id}/pins - pins a KV set to conversation-pinned profile
- PATCH /v1/tenants/{t}/kv-policy - update tenant-level default profile
- GET /v1/conversations/{id}/kv-metadata - returns last-modified, profile, and size estimate

Console features:
- Per-route retention selector with recommended defaults and cost impact estimate.
- Audit log viewer for deletion/export events.
- Simulation view: shows estimated token savings if KV reuse were enabled for a sample traffic trace.

Operational model and SLOs
-------------------------
Ownership:
- Product: lifecycle profiles and UX.
- Eng-serving-runtime: runtime enforcement and compatibility with variants.
- Eng-sre: operational SLOs and runbooks for emergency data removal.

Service-level targets (initial):
- KV-policy-change propagate time: < 2 minutes (99th percentile) for hosted control plane changes.
- Deletion guarantee: queued for deletion within 30 minutes, fully purged across caches within 24 hours for ephemeral/session profiles.
- Audit export availability: 24/7 with 99.9% successful retrieval SLA for the last 90 days.

Telemetry and observability
-------------------------
Required telemetry events:
- kv.policy.assigned (tenant, route, profile)
- kv.item.created (size_bytes, tokens_estimate, profile)
- kv.item.evicted (reason=ttl/space/manual/variant-mismatch)
- kv.item.deleted (deletion_type=automatic/manual/export)

Dashboards:
- KV storage by tenant and route (rolling 30-day), with cost estimate by cost-class.
- Eviction heatmap (time-of-day, tenant, model-variant).
- Compliance incidents (manual deletion/export requests and response times).

Compatibility and variant behavior
----------------------------------
- The runtime will attach a small profile header to requests forwarded to a model variant describing the profile and expected KV shape. Variants that require stricter KV (e.g., full-precision KV) will return a compatibility hint and the orchestrator can choose to:
  a) promote the request to an appropriate variant, or
  b) fall back to re-encoding the required prefix with an estimated cost impact.

Security and compliance considerations
-------------------------------------
- All persisted KV profiles must honor tenant KMS keys where configured.
- Delete and export flows must be auditable with a tamper-evident event stream.
- For Private deployments, provide an operator-controlled retention controller with a UI toggle for legal holds.

Rollout plan
------------
1. Alpha (Hosted only, opt-in tenant flag, Q3 2026): API surface, Console selector, telemetry.
2. Beta (Hosted & Dedicated, default session->2h mapping, Q1 2027): add per-route controls, audit export.
3. GA (All tiers, including Private operator package, Q3 2027): hardened deletion windows, SLO contracts, and billing integration.

Migration and customer impact matrix
-----------------------------------
- Existing tenants with no explicit policy: remain on current implicit behavior until they opt in; will receive Console prompts explaining benefits and cost impact.
- Tenants using long-running playgrounds: recommended to move to ephemeral for cost savings.
- Enterprise tenants: migration playbook includes a pre-rollout simulation and a one-week monitoring window.

Open questions and risks
-----------------------
- Quantifying re-encoding cost for fallback flows requires improved token-estimation signals from the runtime. (Action: engineering spike Q3 2026).
- Legal hold semantics in Private deployments may require additional tooling for offline operator workflows.
- Edge and lightweight runtimes: need a simplified policy surface for constrained storage.

Deliverables and milestones (high level)
---------------------------------------
- API spec and OpenAPI definitions for KV policy endpoints (owner: product) - deliverable Q3 2026.
- Console controls and estimates UX (owner: DX) - prototype Q3 2026, ship Beta Q1 2027.
- Runtime enforcement, telemetry events, and SLOs (owner: eng-serving-runtime & eng-sre) - Alpha Q3 2026, GA Q3 2027.

Appendix: example policy YAML
---------------------------
The following is an example tenant-level policy expressed for readability.

```
default_profile: session
profiles:
  ephemeral:
    ttl_minutes: 5
    deletion_window_hours: 1
    billing_class: S
  session:
    ttl_minutes: 120
    deletion_window_hours: 24
    billing_class: M
  conversation_pinned:
    ttl_days: 30
    deletion_window_hours: 72
    export_enabled: true
    billing_class: L
```
